questions.question: What are the four universal building blocks that almost every program is built from?
questions.explanation: Nearly all program logic, no matter the language, can be described as ordered sequence, stored variables, conditional branching, and repeating loops.

questions.question: An engineer says a feature is 'stuck in an infinite loop.' What does that mean?
options: The program has too many variables
A loop's stopping condition is never satisfied, so it keeps repeating forever
questions.explanation: An infinite loop occurs when the condition meant to stop a loop never becomes true, so the instructions inside it repeat indefinitely.

questions.question: An engineer reports a bug and says 'it's an off-by-one error.' Which question best helps a TPM understand the actual issue?
options: Can we just restart the server?
What's the actual boundary condition that's wrong — is the loop or check running one time too many or too few?
Why does the code have any loops at all?
Can we switch to a different programming language?
questions.explanation: Off-by-one errors are precise: they mean a loop or comparison is evaluated at the wrong boundary (e.g. using <= instead of <), and asking about the exact boundary condition gets to the root cause fastest.
